clue.text: Good book trading centre in Greater Paris area

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces sit inside the word meaning greater

parts.note: greater means more
NT, the New Testament, is a book of the Bible, the Good Book
a mart is a market, a trading centre

explanation.surface: A guidebook entry about a commercial hub somewhere in the Greater Paris region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greater Paris' reads as one phrase, but 'Greater' is MORE, which takes in NT and MART.
explanation.definitionFit: Montmartre is the hilltop district of northern Paris famous for artists and the Sacré-Cœur.

clue.text: Yuppie flu going round work causes misery

indicators.note: going round says the illness letters wrap round the work word

parts.note: yuppie flu is a dismissive name for ME, chronic fatigue syndrome
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Chronic fatigue spreading through the office brings misery.
explanation.definitionFit: A mope is a gloomy listless state or person, akin to wretchedness.

clue.text: Can't use bananas for fruitcake

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A baker says bananas will not do in a fruitcake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' and 'fruitcake' both look like ingredients; one is the anagram signal, the other slang for a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruitcake and nutcase are both slang for a crazy person.

clue.text: Ship's officer's mum seconds calls to arrest a sailor

parts.note: mum, mother, is ma

indicators.note: to arrest means to hold, so the sailor pieces are held inside

parts.note: to call something is to term it
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A naval officer's mother backs calls for a sailor to be arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' reads as backs, supports; it is S.
explanation.definitionFit: A master-at-arms is the ship's officer responsible for discipline and policing aboard.

clue.text: Old magistrates deliver severe thrashing

indicators.note: thrashing means beating about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Old-time magistrates dish out a severe beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeves were local officials in medieval England with magisterial powers.

clue.text: American native ignoring British in Essex town

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving the British letter out

parts.note: Braintree is a market town in Essex, an English county

explanation.surface: A Native American visiting an Essex town pays no attention to the British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American native' looks like a person; it is a tree native to tropical America.
explanation.definitionFit: The rain tree, Samanea saman, is a large tree native to tropical America.

clue.text: French director putting over line from The Lace Maker?

indicators.note: putting over asks for the words to be turned round, read from the other end

parts.note: a lace maker tats, so her line, the words she might say, is 'I tat'

explanation.surface: A film critic notes a French director borrowing a line from the film The Lace Maker.
explanation.walkthrough: To tat is to make lace by hand. 'I tat' turned round gives the director's name; The Lace Maker really is a French film, by another director, which sells the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Tati was the French film director and comic actor behind Monsieur Hulot.

clue.text: One minute reserved by top-notch broadcaster?

definitions.text: One minute reserved by top-notch broadcaster?

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written with the 1 as I

indicators.note: reserved by means held inside, so the one and minute letters sit inside the broadcaster

parts.note: RTE is the Irish state broadcaster
I, the Roman numeral, is one

explanation.surface: A quality broadcaster books just one minute of slot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: a minute booked on a broadcaster is airtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Airtime is broadcasting time allotted on radio or television, booked by the minute.

clue.text: Confession from bride at Savoy causing agitation

parts.note: a confession begins by owning up, 'I am', shortened to I'm
Patience is the heroine, ended up a bride, of the Gilbert and Sullivan opera staged at the Savoy Theatre

explanation.surface: A bride at the Savoy Hotel makes an admission that causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: Savoy suggests the London hotel; it is the theatre of the Savoy operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatience is restless eagerness, a state of agitation at delay.

clue.text: Exotic oriental sea trip is in store for Brownies?

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters are made strange by rearranging them

parts.note: E, east, is the oriental direction

explanation.surface: An exotic eastern cruise is in prospect for a group of Brownie Guides.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies looks like the junior Girl Guides; the question mark admits it means chocolate cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A patisserie is a cake shop, where chocolate brownies might be sold.

clue.text: One of three basic subjects in Ginger's homework

indicators.note: in places the subject's letter inside the word for ginger

parts.note: ginger as a verb means liven up, and pep is liveliness or vigour
the three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so one of them is R

explanation.surface: A schoolchild named Ginger does homework on one of the three basic school subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger' looks like a nickname but is pep, energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Prep, short for preparation, is the British school word for homework.

clue.text: Cycling across the fields?

parts.note: suggests riding a bicycle over farmland, but means farm plantings changed in a repeating cycle field by field

explanation.surface: Someone goes cycling over farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers grow different plants in a field in a regular sequence of seasons.

clue.text: One has coloured flags on the deck

definitions.text: One has coloured flags on the deck

parts.words: One has coloured flags on the deck
parts.note: reads as a sailor running up signal flags on a ship's deck, but the flags are paving flagstones coloured in chalk on the ground

explanation.surface: A sailor runs colourful signal flags up on the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: A flag is also a flagstone, and the deck is slang for the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Street chalk artists draw coloured pictures on the paving stones for passers-by's coins.

clue.text: News about game shows with actors

parts.note: to sport something is to show it off
the actors in a play are the cast

explanation.surface: A news item about television game shows featuring actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game shows' reads as one phrase; 'game' ends the definition and 'shows' gives SPORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportscast is a broadcast of sports news, reporting on games.

clue.text: Call back with one penny" he might have told customer

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral, stands for one

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for call in the other direction

parts.note: to call is to name

explanation.surface: A vendor tells a customer to come back again once they have a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme, Simple Simon met a pieman who wanted to see his penny before handing over a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: A street seller of pies would demand payment from a customer like Simple Simon.

clue.text: Television audience's still needed for oft-rehearsed play

parts.note: a television is a TV set

indicators.note: what an audience hears, so the next word is used for its sound

parts.note: still as a noun means quiet or calm, peace

explanation.surface: A TV studio audience must keep still during a carefully rehearsed show.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a set piece is a practised move from a free kick or corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A set piece in sport is a pre-planned, practised move from a dead-ball situation.

clue.text: Aliases German writer involved in leak turns up

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the whole is read from bottom to top
involved in places the writer inside the leak word

parts.note: to seep is to leak
Thomas Mann was a German novelist

explanation.surface: A German author is caught up in a leak of false names.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen names are pseudonyms authors write under, a kind of alias.

clue.text: One doing over salesman's leading consumer

indicators.note: leading puts the salesman word in front of the consumer word

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
an eater consumes food

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman turns out to be the biggest customer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something over is repeating it, so one who does it over repeats.

clue.text: Expert playing East German college supremo

parts.note: a pro is an expert
playing a team is being versus it, abbreviated V
Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: An expert takes on an East German head of college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' reads as a nationality; it is the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: A provost is the head of certain colleges, at Oxford, Cambridge and elsewhere.

clue.text: Protect pitch, leaving regular bits in lines?

indicators.note: keeping only the evenly spaced letters, first, third, fifth and so on, of the two words

explanation.surface: Groundstaff protect a pitch, leaving bits of it covered at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' reads as cricket or painted markings; it means lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something written in lines of verse is poetic, in the form of poetry.

clue.text: Travel as far as America, going round one state, and half of several others

parts.note: as far as means to, up to a point

indicators.note: going round means the America letters enclose the state

parts.note: US is the United States of America
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island
M is half the two-letter postal code of several other states, such as MA, ME, MI and MO

explanation.surface: A traveller goes as far as America, touring one state and half a dozen more.
explanation.walkthrough: Several US state codes begin with M (Maine ME, Montana MT), so M is half of each.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourism is the business of travel for pleasure.

clue.text: Drug one samples that can get you a bit higher

definitions.text: that can get you a bit higher

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, a drug
one who tries or samples

explanation.surface: A drug one experiments with gets you a little high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Higher' suggests a drug high; it means climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: An étrier is a short rope ladder used by climbers to gain height.

clue.text: Leaves creating such a hoo-hah?

parts.note: tea leaves stirred up in a small vessel make a great fuss over very little

explanation.surface: Someone quits a job and causes a big fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, departs, but it is tea leaves whirling in a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a great commotion over a trivial matter.

clue.text: Ear's not twitching?

parts.note: not, nothing, is nought, O
a tic is a twitching of the muscles

explanation.surface: Someone notes their ear is not twitching.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits stretching 'not' to O, nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the medical adjective meaning relating to the ear.

clue.text: Swear when wife's forgotten name for flower

indicators.note: forgotten means the wife letter is left out

parts.note: to swear is to avow
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone curses on realising they have forgotten the name of a flower for their wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a river, a thing that flows: the Avon of Stratford.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a flower is something that flows, a river such as the Avon.

clue.text: As believer in experience, I tip crimes to explode

indicators.note: to explode means the letters are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: An informant, trusting experience, tips off crimes so they blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: An empiricist holds that knowledge comes from sensory experience rather than reason alone.

clue.text: Pair of braces for speaker's outfit

indicators.note: as said by a speaker, so we go by the sound of the words

parts.note: a brace is two, so a pair of braces is two twos

explanation.surface: Someone buys a pair of braces to go with their outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Braces' looks like trouser straps, but a brace is a pair, as in a brace of pheasants.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the short stiff skirt worn as a ballerina's costume.

clue.text: Head of cookery's dismissed for whacking

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of the cookery word
dismissed means that leading letter is sent away

parts.note: gastronomic means of good cooking and eating

explanation.surface: A head chef is sacked for hitting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whacking' reads as hitting; it is the informal adjective for huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Whacking as an informal adjective means huge, enormously large like astronomical figures.
